themes_detail.label: Tree Maintenance Crisis Emerges
themes_detail.summary: New Tree Requests spiked to 5 complaints THIS WEEK versus 0.1 weekly average over 8 weeks (3900% increase, z-score 14.74), suggesting residents are urgently demanding tree services—a signal that aligns with the community board's repeated multi-year requests for forestry services and street tree maintenance funding.
evidence: 5 New Tree Request complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (3900% spike)
z-score of 14.74 indicates statistically extreme anomaly
Community Board has requested forestry services and street tree maintenance funding for multiple consecutive years—unmet need
reporting_angles: Why did tree service complaints explode this week? Interview residents about what triggered the surge (storm damage, overgrown streets, safety hazards).
Investigate whether Parks Department has capacity to respond to this sudden demand surge or if there's a backlog.

themes_detail.label: Street and Sidewalk Noise Spike
themes_detail.summary: Noise - Street/Sidewalk complaints jumped to 12 THIS WEEK versus 3.6 weekly average (231% increase, z-score 3.42), marking the most recent noise escalation in the district and suggesting a specific new source or pattern of disruption.
evidence: 12 Noise - Street/Sidewalk complaints THIS WEEK vs. 3.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (231% spike)
z-score of 3.42 indicates statistically significant deviation
Timing coincides with other non-emergency police and maintenance complaints spiking this week
reporting_angles: What specific streets or areas are generating the noise surge? Talk to residents about source (construction, traffic, late-night gatherings).
Compare this spike to Police Department enforcement data to see if there's a disconnect between complaints and response.

themes_detail.label: Maintenance and Facility Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Maintenance or Facility complaints doubled to 10 THIS WEEK versus 4.5 weekly average (122% increase, z-score 3.67), the most recent spike, suggesting accelerating infrastructure or public facility problems across the district.
evidence: 10 Maintenance or Facility complaints THIS WEEK vs. 4.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (122% spike)
z-score of 3.67 indicates statistically significant deviation
Converges with street sign and lot condition spikes from 2 weeks ago, suggesting sustained deterioration across public infrastructure
reporting_angles: Map the specific facilities and infrastructure generating complaints this week—are they clustered in one area or district-wide?
Connect to community board's long-standing requests for street reconstruction and facility funding; investigate whether underinvestment is reaching a breaking point.

themes_detail.label: Non-Emergency Police Calls Surge
themes_detail.summary: Non-Emergency Police Matter complaints rose to 14 LAST WEEK versus 6.8 weekly average (107% increase, z-score 4.23), indicating a spike in low-level police matters that may reflect safety concerns or quality-of-life issues the district is escalating to law enforcement.
evidence: 14 Non-Emergency Police Matter complaints LAST WEEK vs. 6.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (107% spike)
z-score of 4.23 indicates statistically significant deviation
Aligns with community board's repeated requests for increased NYPD facility/precinct funding, suggesting residents view policing as understaffed
reporting_angles: What categories of non-emergency complaints drove the surge? Disorderly conduct, trespassing, quality-of-life violations?
Interview NYPD and residents about whether the district feels under-policed and whether the surge reflects actual crime increase or deferred complaints from prior weeks.

themes_detail.label: Illegal Dumping and Lot Neglect
themes_detail.summary: Lot Condition complaints spiked 4 cases TWO WEEKS AGO versus 0.4 weekly average (967% increase, z-score 5.21), and the community board has repeatedly requested increased enforcement of illegal dumping laws—suggesting a persistent environmental quality problem that may be escalating.
evidence: 4 Lot Condition complaints TWO WEEKS AGO vs. 0.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (967% spike)
z-score of 5.21 indicates statistically extreme anomaly
Community Board has submitted repeated multi-year budget requests for increased illegal dumping enforcement—suggests unmet chronic problem
reporting_angles: Identify which lots or neighborhoods are being dumped on and why enforcement has been insufficient to deter it.
Investigate whether the spike reflects a specific incident (e.g., closure of a disposal facility) or systematic underenforcement of dumping laws.
